translations./garage/heading: Give RO-1 Its First Pair of Eyes
translations./garage/brief: A transparent door stands beyond the exit. Choose a LiDAR so RO-1 can discover that the route is not empty.
translations./prediction/heading: What Reveals the Glass Door Sooner?
translations./prediction/hint: Range determines how far you see; refresh rate determines how often you get new measurements.
translations./prediction/choices/0/text: Maximum range is all that matters
translations./prediction/choices/0/feedback: Seeing far isn’t enough—timely updates matter. When you’re close to an obstacle, the gap between scans is critical.
translations./prediction/choices/1/text: Range and refresh rate both matter
translations./prediction/choices/1/feedback: Record your prediction. During the run, watch when scan points appear and how much braking room RO-1 keeps.
translations./prediction/choices/2/feedback: The map stores prior knowledge; sensors turn the current environment into measurements.
translations./running/heading: Stop Safely Before the Glass Door
translations./running/normal_line: RO-1: The LiDAR is scanning. I’ll park in the safe zone.
translations./running/detected_line: RO-1: Echoes are steady ahead; I’m controlling braking now.
translations./debrief/success_summary: A range measurement turns the transparent glass door into evidence RO-1 can act on.
translations./debrief/failure_summary: Compare range, refresh rate, and braking distance, then choose again.
translations./debrief/evidence_caption: The scan points and stopping position both come from this run.
